campbell.title: Campbell City Council — August 18, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered several administrative items, including naming voting delegates for the 2026 League of California Cities annual conference, amending an agreement for city clerk services, and accepting a grant on behalf of the police department. The council also took up an item related to governance around the BART Silicon Valley project.
keyTopics: Designation of voting delegates for the 2026 League of California Cities annual conference
Resolution amending the first amended agreement for city clerk services
Grant acceptance on behalf of the police department, presented by a police captain
Governance matters related to the BART Silicon Valley project

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — August 19, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council took up a routine mix of budget, contract, and infrastructure items, including janitorial and irrigation maintenance contracts, a GIS consultant contract amendment, and a playground replacement project at Bellgrove Park. The Council also considered a five-year law enforcement agreement with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office, a contested appeal of a Planning Commission decision on a 25-lot subdivision on Pierce Road, and several final map approvals for lot splits around the city.
keyTopics: Appeal of Planning Commission's denial of a 25-lot residential subdivision on a 72.45-acre Pierce Road parcel, including its Environmental Impact Report
Five-year law enforcement services agreement with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office
Bellgrove Park playground replacement contracts and a new No Parking Anytime zone on Chester Avenue and Arcadia Palms Drive
Facility electrification purchase for the Warner Hutton House, Civic Center Theater, and Joan Pisani Community Center to replace aging gas equipment
Final map approvals for lot splits at 19200 Shubert Drive, 12468 Ted Avenue, and El Camino Senda

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — August 25, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council considered routine business including a treasurer's report and roof replacement contract for the History Museum, along with two significant housing developments seeking approval for condominium projects on First Street and Sherwood/Acacia Avenue. The Council also held a public hearing on a resident petition to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street, and addressed several infrastructure projects including EV chargers at the maintenance yard and completion of the Woodland Library patio expansion.
keyTopics: Public hearing on renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street, with options to act directly or refer to the Historical Commission for further study
Vesting tentative map approval for 19 condominium units at 349 First Street
Vesting tentative map approval for 33 condominium units at Sherwood and Acacia Avenues
Contract award for History Museum roof replacement (not-to-exceed $147,500) and Maintenance Yard EV Chargers project (not-to-exceed $363,220)
Draft responses to Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's BART Silicon Valley Phase II oversight

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 18, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council took up a routine mix of business, including approving past meeting minutes, financial reports, and payment records, along with a professional services agreement and an amendment to an existing contract. The Council also considered a Town Code cleanup ordinance, appointed a voting delegate for an upcoming League of California Cities event, and addressed a request related to continuing a public hearing on appeals.
keyTopics: Approval of the August 4, 2026 Town Council meeting minutes
Monthly financial and investment report for June 2026, plus accounts payable and payroll reports
Agreement for professional services and a second amendment to an existing agreement
Appointment of a voting delegate and alternate for the League of California Cities Annual meeting
Omnibus ordinance making minor updates to the Town Code, and a request to continue or hear a public hearing on appeals

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — August 26, 2026
san-jose.summary: This was a procedural Rules and Open Government Committee meeting focused on organizing upcoming City Council agendas rather than debating policy. The Committee reviewed the final agenda for the September 1, 2026 Council meeting and considered a VEBA Advisory Committee appointment, while the September 8 meeting was cancelled.
keyTopics: Review and finalization of the September 1, 2026 Council meeting agenda, including possible new items and time-certain scheduling
Cancellation of the September 8, 2026 draft agenda review
Public record covering August 13–20, 2026
VEBA Advisory Committee appointment
Joint special meeting planning with the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — August 25, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council held a closed session to discuss performance evaluations for two Council-appointed staff positions and related labor negotiation matters. The meeting also included a period for public comments on topics not otherwise on the agenda.
keyTopics: Public comment period for non-agenda items
Performance evaluation of the City Clerk and City Manager
Labor negotiation discussion involving the City Clerk and City Manager as unrepresented employees, with Vice Mayor Clark as the designated negotiator

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a closed session meeting to discuss confidential matters not detailed on the public agenda, followed by a special meeting featuring a presentation on the CleanWater Program update.
keyTopics: Closed session discussion (details confidential)
CleanWater Program update presentation

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: Cupertino's Teen Commission met to discuss plans for a Bike Fest event, a Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program, and a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI. The Commission also considered approval of minutes from its June 10, 2026 meeting.
keyTopics: Bike Fest planning
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program
Youth-led organization Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in hybrid format, allowing residents to attend in person or participate remotely via Zoom or phone. One Councilmember, Chahal, joined remotely from India for this session.
keyTopics: Councilmember Chahal's remote participation from Panchkula, India
Hybrid meeting format with in-person and remote public participation options via Zoom or phone

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 11, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered an ordinance amending part of the city's municipal code and received an educational presentation on municipal bonds. The meeting also included routine items such as the council calendar, meeting minutes, and upcoming agenda items.
keyTopics: Introduction of an ordinance amending Municipal Code Title XIII, Chapters B.6
Presentation on "Municipal Bonds 101" from Finance staff
Review of the City Council meeting calendar
Approval of past City Council meeting minutes
Preview of anticipated items for the next regular Council meeting

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Public Art Commission — August 20, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Public Art Commission reviewed a proposed public art plan for the 3150 El Camino Real private development, with a presentation from the project's art consultant and artist. The commission also considered funding for temporary interactive media art installations, and looked at accepting donated artworks from two local artists into the city's public art collection.
keyTopics: Approval of June 18, 2026 meeting minutes
Public art plan for 3150 El Camino Real, presented by art consultant Danielle Wohl, artist Giles Miller, and Acclaim Companies
Up to $70,000 in funding for Code:ART 2027 temporary interactive media installations
Acceptance of donated artworks by CASP artists Adrienne Defendi and Eric Fei
